recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If the legacy DAF medication product form ValueSet is ever brought back into build scope, address its NCImeta system URI under a separate medication/terminology cleanup issue rather than reopening this completed page-removal decision.
issue_request: FHIR-31938 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core vocab change request for R5 asking to remove the "Using the NCI Metathesaurus with FHIR" page because NCImeta is not a code system and should not be presented for Coding.system use.
initial_application: Commit 2c4f6306e8c47abf78ce9ba3e05bd032bfa17636 applied FHIR-31938 by deleting source/ncimeta.html and removing ncimeta.html from publish.ini, source/hierarchy.xml, source/terminologies-systems.html, and source/valueset/valueset-notes.xml.
additional_context: FHIR-17778 records the related earlier no-change decision that Using Terminology pages were moving out of core and the NCIM page would not be moved. FHIR-37853 later removed the residual NCImeta row from source/terminologies-systems.html while making THO authoritative for external terminology details. Vocab minutes on 2022-08-08 state FHIR-31938 had been resolved during the 2022-08-04 main WG call and applied. The only remaining current-source NCImeta URI is in legacy source/medication/valueset-medication-productform.xml, which is not in source/fhir.ini active [valuesets], is not referenced by the Medication binding, and has no tracked generated publish artifact.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. No source edit was needed because the in-build NCImeta page, navigation, filter reference, and code-system list entry are already gone.

related_jiras.note: Earlier no-change issue established that NCIM was not NCI Thesaurus and that the NCIM page would not move to THO.
Removed external code-system rows without current Using Terminology links, including the remaining NCImeta row, as part of making THO authoritative.
Later removed terminology NamingSystem example bundles to avoid stale core copies of terminology identifiers.
